problem: writeExportFile swallows any mkdir/writeFile failure (it only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and returns normally. Its only caller, runHistoryExport (line 122), then prints `exported N run(s) to <file>` at line 131 and exits 0. That is the silent catch error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1 forbids: the caller goes on as if the write succeeded.
impact: A user or script exporting to a read-only or invalid path is told the file was written, with exit code 0. Nothing is on disk, and the failure is invisible unless KERYX_VERBOSE is set. Fix: let the error propagate, or rethrow with `cannot write export to ${file}` and `{ cause: error }`. Enumeration: two catches in the new file, lines 68 and 127. The one at 127 is a commented display-only fallback and is fine.

problem: The rethrow drops the original error: there is no `cause`, and the caught `error` is never used. The message also omits the input (cwd / runs log path). This breaks error-handling.mdc Rule 2 and Rule 5 / Iron Law 3.
impact: Whoever debugs a failed export sees only 'could not read the runs log', with no underlying ENOENT/EACCES/parse error or stack and no path.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: The command-label normalization chain (collapse CR/LF, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is duplicated three times in this change: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53, wiki-history-export.ts:56-60 and wiki-history.ts:47-51. Only the constant was shared, not the function.
impact: A change to how labels are clipped or cleaned must be made in three places. If one is missed, terminal output, CSV and markdown drift apart. Extract one `commandLabel(command)` helper next to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH and call it from all three sites.

problem: Stale doc comment. It says collectRunRows 'Returns the runs oldest first', but the function only filters listWikiRuns, which is documented and implemented as newest first (src/wiki/history.ts:495, sort at :508). The comment asserts an ordering the code never produces.
impact: Readers and callers trust a wrong ordering contract, and the exported file lists runs newest first, the opposite of the stated intent. Either reverse the result or fix the comment.
quote:
Returns the runs
 * oldest first, so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened.

problem: renderRunLine takes a boolean flag that picks between two different renderers (markdown vs CSV), so call sites read `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`. It also has 4 positional parameters, and `pages` duplicates `run.pages`, which the only caller (line 119) passes straight back in. The two branches share no code apart from the duplicated label block.
impact: Call sites are hard to read, and adding a third format means another flag or a widened signature. Split it into renderCsvLine / renderMdLine, or dispatch on RunExportFormat, and drop the redundant `pages` argument.

problem: runHistoryExport is about 57 lines and does separable jobs at mixed levels: argument parsing and validation (target, --format inference, --since date parsing), the row transform (timestamp trimming and rendering, lines 116-120), file I/O (line 122) and the result report. Formatting the data sits inline in the same function that writes it (the 'I/O mixed with a transform' threshold).
impact: The rendering cannot be unit-tested without the filesystem and argv, and each new option grows this one function. Move option parsing into a `parseExportOptions(args)` helper and rendering into a pure `renderExport(runs, format)` called by the I/O shell.

problem: The --export usage is documented three ways in this change. HISTORY_USAGE leaves out --since and --command, while EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:19) and the `keryx wiki` help in wiki.ts list them. Two places document one behaviour differently.
impact: Users reading `wiki history` usage don't learn about the filters. Every future flag must be added to three strings by hand. Derive HISTORY_USAGE from EXPORT_USAGE, or reference it.
quote: "Usage: keryx wiki history <page> | keryx wiki history --runs [--json] [--export <file> [--format csv|md]]"

problem: The file rebuilds WikiRunSummary from listWikiRuns' return type when src/wiki/history.ts:488 already exports the interface. It is a second name and definition path for one concept. This is stylistic, because the service facade may simply not re-export the type.
impact: Small indirection. Re-exporting the type from ../wiki/service would make the dependency explicit.
